W2 (empirical), after E014. Best remains E010: 6.639 s, 0.7548 (8.5 ep, Muon+EMA+prog-res 24/28/32, last width 512). The margin over the 0.753 bar is 0.17 pp.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 exact rerun of E010: bit-identical accuracy, time within 0.1%. E013 LS 0.2: 0.7551/6.630. E014 Muon lr x1.5: 0.7557/6.631.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves about 4.8% time. Roughly linear (E007 to E008).
2. Compile saved about 4% once the stride recompile leak was fixed (E003 to E004).
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s (E004 to E005). The cheapest gain.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E005 to E006).
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp. Time tracks pixel count.
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp, about the epoch-dial exchange rate.
7. LR floor 0 on top of EMA: no gain (E009).
8. Resolution cliff (E011): -14% time for -1.4 pp.
9. Loss and optimizer-scale knobs (LS 0.3 to 0.2: +0.04 pp; Muon lr x1.5: +0.1 pp) are flat and inside noise. The hyperparameters are near a plateau, and time is unchanged by them.
10. Noise: runs are deterministic per seed. Seed and recipe-reshuffle noise is about ±0.2 pp on 3-seed means. Time noise is about 1% or less. Fixed costs are about 0.3-0.5 s.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing, and over-predicted E009 and E011 accuracy. Lesson: centre accuracy-neutral changes on 0.7548-0.7555 and keep time at 6.63-6.64.

Unsure: GPU idle and launch overhead under 4 CPUs. Steps are large (25 per epoch at batch 2000), so CUDA graphs probably save only 0-6%. Muon's Newton-Schulz on many small matrices and the Python LR loops may be launch-bound. Also unsure whether plain EMA matches Lookahead, and what the held-out seed spread is. Accuracy gains cannot buy time unless they are spent on epochs (0.18 pp per 4.8% of time); the remaining slack is only about 0.17 pp.

forecasts.reason: Steps are large so launch overhead is small; the graph gain is probably 0-6%, and capture complexity (multiple resolutions, Muon) risks no gain. The math is identical, so accuracy stays the same.
Other scalar knobs (LS, Muon lr) moved less than 0.1 pp; the weight decay change is likely also within noise, and time is unchanged.
Removing host syncs and Python LR loops probably saves 1-3%. Accuracy is identical in principle, but a changed op order may reshuffle it by a small amount.
Lookahead resets give a regularizing trajectory effect; plain EMA likely recovers most but not all of the gain, and the margin is thin, so the accuracy centre is slightly lower than the tip.

cruxes: What fraction of the 6.64 s is GPU idle time from launch or host-sync overhead (a profiler trace)? This decides whether CUDA graphs or graph-break removal can give 5% or more.
Does a plain EMA match Lookahead? If it does not, the Lookahead trajectory is a regularizer, and the accuracy margin needed to cut epochs depends on it.
What are the held-out-seed (3-12) mean and std at E010? If the 10-seed mean is below 0.753, the tip is fragile and no epoch cut is safe.
